label: copy phase (after <DEL>), dense; strongest on early copy steps with fed-back p
explanation: Broad copy-phase feature: fires at about 95% of copy steps (t > L, recall_idx >= 1) and almost never during the original tokens or at the <DEL> step itself (orig/delimiter steps hold ~0% of the mass; the few original-phase activations are tiny and come late in long sequences). It is not specific to token identity: rate is flat (~0.85) across out_tok/in_tok/first_tok, L, and n_digits. Magnitude is modulated by the fed-back input: when the input is p the feature fires about 2.5x harder (in_tok=p holds 8% of the mass versus ~3% for other tokens), and q/b/f/1 are also somewhat elevated. The top activations (~6.3) all occur at the first copy steps when the echoed input is p (e.g. s p p p <DEL> s [p]). Steps that are inactive inside the copy phase are low-magnitude cases spread over sequences, with no clean rule found. Dev F1 0.975, mass recall 0.9997.

issues: Label overclaims 'strongest on early copy steps'. Average magnitude does not depend on position. For in_tok=p, recall_idx<=3 has mass/recall = 0.0431/0.0190 = 2.27x, and recall_idx>3 has 0.0369/0.0159 = 2.32x. Across all copy steps it is 1.03x early versus 0.97x late. Only the top-12 examples happen to fall at early steps (mostly recall_idx 2-3).
The firing rate is flat across in_tok (0.93-0.97), with two exceptions: p (1.000) and q (0.997) almost always fire. Small, but worth stating. q also carries raised mass (1.23x per step).

No systematic class of false positives was found. The copy-phase firing rate stays at 0.94-0.96 across every split tried: recall_idx==1 (0.940), to_go==0 (0.957), L==3 (0.941), L==9 (0.959), in_count>=2 (0.948), repeated input (0.953), p in the sequence (0.968), and neither p nor q in the sequence (0.945). The roughly 5% of off steps look like scattered noise.
The missed activations on the test split (3147 steps on original tokens) hold 0.0% of the mass and are tiny (<=0.06 relative). That is negligible.

Extra finding beyond the explanation: activation stays raised for a few copy steps after a p has been echoed. seen([p,q]) covers 38% of active steps but 51% of the mass, and the example sequences decay after the p.
